mainTopic: Rabbinic decrees and hide flayed past כדי אחיזה, and the dispute between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן over whether a torn hide is חלים (repairable).
overview: The amud opens as רב יוסף answers רבה's two challenges about rabbinic decrees. The tear in the garment shows why it is pure, and כהנים are careful when they cut the bird עולה. Next the גמרא challenges רבה בר אבוה from our משנה about flaying a hide for a carpet: why is there no גזירה once the hide is flayed past כדי אחיזה? It answers that the משנה deals with טומאה דרבנן, and that the impure animal there is a slaughtered טרפה of קדשים, following אבוה דשמואל. A ברייתא about flaying שרצים is also turned aside: it teaches only about the hide on the neck, following רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The גמרא then returns to the torn garment. רב הונא limits the rule, and ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about whether a torn hide is חלים (repairable). ריש לקיש's view is challenged from straps cut out of a hide, from flaying, and from the neck hide, and each challenge is answered. The amud ends as רבי ירמיה begins a new challenge from an impure oven, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה: then decree on the bird burnt offering too
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his challenge. According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, a bird עולה needs only a majority of the two סימנים cut. So we should make a decree, out of worry that someone will not actually reach the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bird burnt offering according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: let him decree, in case a person comes to not do a majority of the two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is finishing a challenge he began earlier. He argues that if the rabbis worry about mistakes elsewhere, they should also make a גזירה here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that a bird עולה is valid when only the majority of its two סימנים is cut. רבה says that by the same reasoning used elsewhere, we should fear people will cut too little. So we should decree against relying on just a majority. If no such decree exists, the reasoning he is attacking looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a burnt offering
Let him decree (make a rabbinic safeguard)
Perhaps / in case
The majority of the two (סימנים, the windpipe and food pipe)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the second half of רבה's challenge, which started before this section. The first half (about the garment immersed that day) is answered in the next step.

phrases.english: A bird burnt offering
according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, let him decree
phrases.notes: He holds that cutting the majority of the two סימנים is enough for this offering.

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא לָא אָתֵי לְמֶעְבַּד רוֹב שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: lest one come to not do the majority of the two.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹלַת הָעוֹף לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לִיגְזַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's challenge from before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning that calls for a decree out of worry that people will make mistakes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we worry about mistakes in one case, we should also decree in the case of the bird עולה. Since we don't, the reasoning is inconsistent.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the tear itself shows why it is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers the first challenge. No one will mistakenly think a same-day immersion is enough, because the visible tear explains why the garment is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: What you said, that we should decree in case people say that immersion on the same day is enough, is not a concern. Its tear proves about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts answering רבה's two challenges. This step answers the first one, about the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה worried that onlookers would think a garment immersed that very day is already pure. רב יוסף says onlookers can see the tear. So they will understand the garment is pure because of the tear, not because a same-day טבילה works. Since no one will be misled, no גזירה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
An immersion done that same day (before nightfall)
Works / is effective (here it does not mean the offering)
Its tear proves about it (the tear shows the reason)

steps.confusionAlert: The word עוֹלָה here means 'works' or 'counts.' It does not mean the burnt offering mentioned in the step before.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
That which you said, a decree

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ טְבִילָה בַּת יוֹמָא עוֹלָה –
phrases.english: lest they say that a same-day immersion is effective —
its tear proves about it.
phrases.notes: People can see the rip, so they know the garment is pure because of the tear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: דְּקָא אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of רבה's two-part challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: No risk of misunderstanding, so no decree is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Onlookers might think a same-day immersion makes a garment pure
steps.terutzMaskana: The visible tear explains the purity, so no one is misled

steps.title: רב יוסף: priests are careful
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers the second challenge. No decree is needed for the bird עולה, because the כהנים who do the cutting are careful and will surely cut the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what you said, that for the bird burnt offering according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון he should decree: the כהנים are careful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers רבה's second challenge, about the bird offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה feared someone might cut less than the majority. רב יוסף points out that only כהנים do this cutting, and כהנים are careful with מצוות. So the worry does not apply, and no גזירה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Priests are careful (quick and diligent in doing מצוות)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף answers both challenges by showing there is no real risk. The tear explains the garment's purity, and כהנים are careful with the bird offering. Where there is no real risk, there is no need for a גזירה.

phrases.english: And that which you said,

phrases.aramaic: עוֹלַת הָעוֹף לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לִיגְזַר –
phrases.english: a bird burnt offering according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, let him decree —
priests are careful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of רבה's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: The people who perform the act are reliable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone might cut less than the majority of the סימנים
steps.terutzMaskana: כהנים are careful, so there is no need to decree

steps.title: Come and hear: flaying a hide for a carpet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רבה בר אבוה's explanation of the משנה in כלים. It quotes our משנה: when someone flays any animal to use the hide as a carpet, the measure is enough to hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who flays a domesticated animal or a wild animal, an impure one or a pure one, a small one or a large one, for a carpet: the measure is enough to grasp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It starts by quoting our משנה, which it will use against רבה בר אבוה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when the hide is meant to become a carpet, the key measure is כדי אחיזה, enough skin peeled to grab hold of. Until then, the hide still counts as part of the flesh. The גמרא is about to show that this measure clashes with how רבה בר אבוה explained the משנה in כלים.

keyTerms.meaning: One who flays (peels the hide off an animal)
Small and large animals
A carpet / spread
Enough to grasp (enough hide peeled off to hold onto)

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the opening quote. The actual question against רבה בר אבוה comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who flays a domesticated animal or a wild animal,
an impure one or a pure one,
a small one or a large one,
for a carpet — the measure is enough to grasp.
phrases.notes: Until that much is peeled, the hide still counts as connected to the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבה–רב יוסף exchange and opens a new challenge from our משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר אבוה's explanation of the משנה in כלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the measure for a carpet (כדי אחיזה) will be compared with his explanation

steps.title: Why not make a decree for a hide flayed more than the grasping measure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from our משנה that once more than כדי אחיזה of the hide is flayed, the hide is טהור. It asks why the חכמים did not decree otherwise, in case someone flays only כדי אחיזה and then touches impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: So once more than a handhold's worth of hide has been flayed, the hide is pure. Why? Let us make a decree, in case the person ends up flaying only a handhold's worth. Then he is really touching impurity, and we would wrongly call him pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it began in step 4. It asks why the חכמים did not make a protective decree here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the hide carries impurity up to כדי אחיזה, so past that point it is טהור. This is the same kind of worry רבה raised earlier: a person might stop short of the real amount. The גמרא asks why no decree was made here either.

keyTerms.meaning: enough of the flayed hide to hold onto, a handhold
let the חכמים make a decree
perhaps, lest; the worry behind a decree
we declare pure

phrases.english: This implies: more than a measure of grasping, it is pure.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading this from the משנה's words in step 4.

phrases.english: Why? Let us decree,
lest he does not end up doing
more than a measure of grasping,
and he is touching impurity,
and we are declaring him pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in step 4 by drawing the inference from the משנה and asking why there is no decree.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling implied by our משנה that a hide flayed beyond כדי אחיזה is טהור, with no protective decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Earlier the גמרא considered decrees for fear a person would not reach the needed amount. The same fear applies here, so a decree should be expected.

steps.title: The משנה is dealing with rabbinic impurity
steps.stepSummary: If Torah-level impurity were involved, a decree would indeed be made. But the משנה deals with טומאה דרבנן, so no extra decree is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we were talking about Torah impurity, you would be right. But what case are we dealing with here? Impurity that is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It narrows the משנה to a case of rabbinic impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that for טומאה דאורייתא the חכמים would make such a decree. Since the impurity here is itself only דרבנן, the חכמים do not add a further decree on top of it.

keyTerms.meaning: impurity by Torah law
impurity by rabbinic law
indeed, so it is; agreeing with the questioner
what case are we dealing with here? It introduces a narrowed reading

phrases.english: If it were Torah-law impurity, indeed so;
here, what are we dealing with?
With rabbinic-law impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה is set in a situation of rabbinic impurity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה covers Torah-level impurity, so a decree should be expected.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deals with טומאה דרבנן, and no extra decree is made for that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the passage. Every case in the משנה must now fit rabbinic impurity.

steps.title: A pure person flaying an impure animal is Torah impurity
steps.stepSummary: The rabbinic-impurity answer works for an impure person flaying a pure animal. But a pure person flaying an impure animal involves a נבלה, which is impure by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for an impure person flaying a pure animal. But a pure person flaying an impure animal involves Torah impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 6. One of the משנה's cases does not seem to fit rabbinic impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An impure person's impurity can be rabbinic, so the first case fits. But an impure animal sounds like a נבלה, and a נבלה is impure by Torah law. So that case cannot be explained as rabbinic impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: this works out well (for one case, but not the other)
an impure person flaying a pure animal
a pure person flaying an impure animal

phrases.english: It works out for an impure person with a pure animal;
but a pure person with an impure animal,
that is Torah-law impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that the משנה deals only with rabbinic impurity.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case of a pure person flaying an impure animal seems to involve a נבלה, which is impure by Torah law.

steps.title: The impure animal is a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The 'impure animal' in the משנה is a properly slaughtered animal that turned out to be a טרפה. Its impurity is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word. The impure animal in the משנה is a טרפה, not a נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slaughtered טרפה is not a נבלה, so it is not impure by Torah law. Any impurity it has is rabbinic. That keeps the משנה inside rabbinic impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal with a fatal defect; here, one that was properly slaughtered

phrases.english: With a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the 'impure animal' is a slaughtered טרפה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The impure animal is a נבלה, which is impure by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a slaughtered טרפה, whose impurity is rabbinic.

steps.title: Can a טרפה make things impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a slaughtered טרפה can make things impure at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a טרפה capable of making things impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. It asks whether a slaughtered טרפה has any impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A properly slaughtered animal is normally not impure, even if it turns out to be a טרפה. If so, a טרפה cannot be the 'impure animal' of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: capable of making things impure

phrases.english: Is a tereifa capable of imparting impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer given in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a slaughtered טרפה can make things impure, so it could count as the 'impure animal' of the משנה.

steps.title: Yes, following אבוה דשמואל about קדשים
steps.stepSummary: Yes. אבוה דשמואל said that a slaughtered טרפה of קדשים makes things impure. So the משנה is talking about a sacrificial animal found to be a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, following the father of שמואל. The father of שמואל said: a טרפה that was slaughtered makes things impure when it is a sacrificial animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting אבוה דשמואל. A slaughtered טרפה of קדשים does make things impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבוה דשמואל rules that a slaughtered טרפה of קדשים imparts impurity, and this impurity is rabbinic. So the משנה's case of a pure person flaying an impure animal involves only rabbinic impurity. That is why no extra decree was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: sacrificial animals, holy things
that one slaughtered

steps.whatToRemember: No decree is made beyond כדי אחיזה because the משנה deals with טומאה דרבנן. The impure person can have rabbinic impurity. The impure animal is a slaughtered טרפה of קדשים, which makes things impure only by rabbinic law, following אבוה דשמואל.

phrases.english: Yes, in accordance with Shmuel's father,
as Shmuel's father said:
A tereifa that one slaughtered
imparts impurity in the case of sacrificial animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 and so supports the answer of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Following אבוה דשמואל, a slaughtered טרפה of קדשים imparts impurity, so the משנה can be about such an animal.

steps.title: A ברייתא about flaying creeping animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: when flaying a שרץ, the hide counts as connected to the flesh until the whole animal is flayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: when someone flays creeping animals, the hide is still connected until he has flayed all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to use as a challenge against רבה בר אבוה. This step only quotes the source. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that by שרצים the hide counts as connected all the way until the end of the flaying. Because it singles out שרצים, the גמרא will next ask what this implies about other animals.

keyTerms.meaning: One who flays, meaning someone removing the hide from an animal
Creeping animals, the small creatures whose dead bodies give off impurity
Connection: the hide is still treated as part of the flesh for impurity

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda
says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
One who flays creeping animals: it is a connection,
phrases.notes: He means the hide still counts as joined to the flesh, so touching the hide is like touching the שרץ.

phrases.english: until he flays all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to test רבה בר אבוה's claim that a decree exists
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר אבוה's explanation that there is a rabbinic decree about hide flayed beyond the grasping measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step sets up the source. The inference that does the attacking comes in the next step.

steps.title: The inference: by a camel the hide is not connected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the ברייתא that by a camel, the hide is not connected once it is flayed past the grasping measure. That would mean there is no decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies: by a camel, it is not a connection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא. Only שרצים stay connected until the end, so by a camel the flayed hide is not connected. This goes against רבה בר אבוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a camel's hide stops being connected once it is flayed past the grasping measure, then the רבנן did not make a decree to keep it impure. רבה בר אבוה said they did, so the ברייתא seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies; it signals a conclusion drawn from what the source left out
Camel, an example of a large non-kosher animal

phrases.english: This implies that by a camel, it is not a connection.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא said this only about שרצים. So the גמרא reads it as excluding other animals, like a camel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only שרצים are connected until fully flayed. So a camel's hide is not connected after partial flaying, which shows there is no decree.

steps.title: The ברייתא only speaks about the hide on the neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. The ברייתא implies only that the neck hide of a camel is not connected, and this follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say it implies that by a camel the hide is not connected. Rather, say it implies that the hide on the neck is not connected, and this follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It reads the ברייתא as teaching something much smaller, so it says nothing against רבה בר אבוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not saying that any partly flayed camel hide is free of impurity. It only teaches the case where everything is flayed except the neck. In that case רבי יוחנן בן נורי in the משנה already says the neck hide is not connected, so the proof against the decree falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say this, rather say that: the גמרא replaces one reading with another
The hide on the neck, the last part left when flaying from the legs

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not deny that a camel can be different from a שרץ. It only narrows what the difference is: the neck hide, not any hide flayed beyond the grasping measure.

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא הָא בְּגָמָל אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר,
phrases.english: Do not say: this implies that by a camel it is not a connection,
rather say:
with the hide that is on the neck, it is not a connection,
and this follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא הָא בְּגָמָל אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר, אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inference drawn in step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the broad reading that a camel's hide is not connected after partial flaying
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's implication is limited to the neck hide, following רבי יוחנן בן נורי. It does not deny the decree.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about שרצים does not disprove רבה בר אבוה. Its implication about a camel is only about the neck hide, following רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

steps.title: A torn garment stays connected if a scarf-sized piece is left
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, quoting רבי שמעון ברבי יוסי, limits the earlier-cited law that a mostly torn garment becomes pure. If an untorn piece the size of a scarf is left, it is still connected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רבי שמעון ברבי יוסי: the law was only taught when he did not leave a scarf-sized piece untorn. But if he left a scarf-sized piece, it is still a connection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier-cited משנה about a torn garment and adds a limit to it. This begins a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that once most of an impure garment is torn, the two halves are no longer connected and the garment is pure. רב הונא says this is true only if what is left untorn is smaller than a scarf. If a scarf-sized piece still holds the garment together, it still counts as one connected garment and stays impure.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when: a phrase that limits a law to a narrower case
He left over, meaning he left a part untorn
The size of a scarf, a piece of cloth big enough to be useful on its own

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that tearing most of a garment is not always enough. What counts is whether a useful piece still holds it together.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yosei:
They taught this only
when he did not leave in it the size of a scarf,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה cited earlier: once most of an impure garment is torn, it becomes pure.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שִׁיֵּיר בָּהּ כְּדֵי מַעְפּוֹרֶת – חִבּוּר.
phrases.english: but if he left in it the size of a scarf, it is a connection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns away from the flaying discussion and returns to limit the earlier-cited משנה about a torn garment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mostly torn garment is pure only if the untorn part is smaller than a scarf. If a scarf-sized piece remains, the garment is still connected and stays impure.

steps.title: Is a torn hide considered repairable?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the rule that a mostly torn item becomes pure applies only to a טלית, because a hide is חלים (repairable). רבי יוחנן says even a hide is not considered repairable.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The rule was taught only about a garment. But a hide can be repaired, so it stays impure. רבי יוחנן said: Even a hide is not considered repairable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement about whether the rule of a torn garment also applies to a torn hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that a garment that is mostly torn becomes pure. ריש לקיש limits this to cloth, because leather can easily be sewn back together, so the tear does not end its status as a usable item. רבי יוחנן holds that a torn hide also becomes pure.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this rule only about (a limiting phrase)
A garment or cloak
Hide, leather
Repairable; it can be fixed and made whole again

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
They taught this only about a garment,
phrases.notes: This refers to the rule we just saw: a garment that is mostly torn becomes pure.

phrases.english: but a hide is repairable.
phrases.notes: Since it can be fixed, a torn hide stays impure.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even a hide is also not repairable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ריש לקיש לא שנו אלא טלית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further limits the rule that a mostly torn garment becomes pure, now asking whether it applies to a hide.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: a torn hide stays impure because it is חלים. רבי יוחנן: a torn hide also becomes pure.

steps.title: Challenge from cutting an impure hide into straps
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a משנה: a hide impure with מדרס that is cut down to less than five טפחים becomes pure according to everyone. Why? According to ריש לקיש it should be repairable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: A hide impure with מדרס, which the owner planned to make into straps and sandals, becomes pure once he puts a knife to it, says רבי יהודה. The חכמים say: Not until he cuts it down to less than five טפחים. At least when he cuts it down, it is pure. Why? Let us say it is repairable!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a משנה that seems to show a cut hide becomes pure, which goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and the חכמים disagree about when the hide becomes pure, but both agree that once it is cut below five טפחים it is pure. If a hide is always חלים like ריש לקיש says, the cut pieces could be sewn back, so why should the hide lose its impurity?

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity caused by a זב or similar person treading, sitting, or lying on an item
He intended, he planned (a use for the item)
A scalpel or cutting knife
Handbreadths (a unit of measure)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan objected to Reish Lakish:
A hide that is impure with treading impurity,
if he planned to make it into straps and sandals,
once he put a knife to it, it is pure,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say:
Not until he reduces it to less than five handbreadths.
At least when he reduces it, it is pure,
Why? Let us say it is repairable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that a torn hide is חלים and stays impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a hide cut below five טפחים is pure according to all. If hide is always repairable, it should stay impure.

steps.title: A straight cut versus a circular cut
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that he only called a hide repairable when it was cut in a straight line. The משנה is talking about cutting around in a circle, which cannot be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said it is repairable, I meant where he cut it in a straight line. Here we are dealing with a case where he cuts it going around in a circle.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself by saying the משנה is about a different kind of cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A straight slit can be sewn back easily, so the hide is still considered whole. Cutting in a circle to make straps is not easy to fix. So in that case even ריש לקיש agrees the hide becomes pure.

keyTerms.meaning: He cut it straight, in a plain line
With what case are we dealing here? (introduces a narrower case)
Cutting or trimming
Around it, in a circle

phrases.english: When I said that it is repairable,
that is where he cut it in a straight line,
here, with what are we dealing?
Where he cuts and goes around it in a circle.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי קאמרי דחלים היכא דקא צרי ליה להדיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about a circular cut
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any cut hide can be sewn back, so it should stay impure according to ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a straight cut is repairable; a circular cut is not, so the hide becomes pure.

steps.title: Challenge from flaying a hide for a carpet
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges ריש לקיש from our משנה: when flaying for a carpet, the hide counts as connected only up to כדי אחיזה. Beyond that it is pure. But the hide could be sewn back, so why is it not still connected?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objected: One who flays a domesticated or wild animal, pure or impure, small or large, for a carpet, the hide is connected up to the measure of grasping. This means more than the measure of grasping is pure. Why? Let us say it is repairable!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to ריש לקיש comes from our משנה about flaying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that once more than כדי אחיזה is flayed, the hide is no longer connected to the flesh for impurity. But if hide is always חלים, the flayed part could be reattached, so it should still count as connected.

keyTerms.meaning: One who flays, skins an animal
A carpet or spread
The measure of grasping: enough hide to hold onto while flaying
Small animal and large animal

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya objected:
One who flays a domesticated animal or a wild animal,
a pure one or an impure one,
a small one or a large one,
for a carpet, the measure of grasping,
this implies that more than the measure of grasping is pure,
But why? Let us say it is repairable!

steps.triggerLanguage: מתיב רבי ירמיה המפשיט בבהמה ובחיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to ריש לקיש, after the first was answered in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that hide is חלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats flayed hide beyond כדי אחיזה as disconnected; if hide is repairable, it should still count as connected.

steps.title: Each flayed piece counts as fallen off
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין explains the משנה: each piece of hide that is flayed is treated as already fallen off, because it will never be put back on the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין explained it: Each piece, one after another, becomes as if it fell off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין answers רבי ירמיה's challenge and defends ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A torn hide is repairable because people do sew torn leather back together. But nobody sews flayed skin back onto an animal. So each flayed piece is seen as gone for good, and it is no longer connected.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, interpreted it
Fallen off; considered detached

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's idea of חלים applies only where people really would fix the item. A straight tear in leather can be sewn, but a circular cut, or skin flayed off an animal, is treated as finished and separated.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin explained it:
Each piece, one after another, becomes fallen off.

steps.triggerLanguage: תרגמה רבי אבין ראשון ראשון עושה ניפול
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: flayed skin is never reattached
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Flayed hide, like torn hide, could be considered repairable and still connected.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each flayed piece is treated as fallen off since it will never be reattached, so it is not connected.

steps.title: Challenge from the hide on the neck
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges ריש לקיש: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the hide over the neck is not connected. But that hide is still attached, so according to ריש לקיש it should surely count as connected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: About the hide on the neck, רבי יוחנן בן נורי says it is not connected. Why not? It is still standing there in a 'repaired' state!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a new challenge against ריש לקיש from another line in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said a torn hide that can be sewn back still counts as connected. The neck hide was never even torn; it is still fully in place. So if a fixable hide counts as connected, this hide should count all the more, yet רבי יוחנן בן נורי says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The hide that covers the animal's neck
Connection: counting as attached for טומאה
It stands whole, as if already repaired

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raises an objection:
The hide that is on the neck,
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says
it is not a connection.
Why? It stands there whole!
phrases.notes: The neck hide was never torn off, so it is even better than a hide that could be sewn back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to ריש לקיש after רבי אבין answered רבי ירמיה's challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a repairable hide still counts as connected
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: a hide that never came off should count as connected even more than a torn hide that can be fixed, yet רבי יוחנן בן נורי says it is not connected.

steps.title: אביי points to the other opinion in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the challenge: the same משנה also quotes the חכמים, who say the neck hide is connected, and that fits ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Look at the next part of the משנה: 'And the חכמים say: it is a connection.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's challenge by pointing to the next line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using רב יוסף's own reasoning, the חכמים would support ריש לקיש. So the משנה cannot be a clear proof against him, because ריש לקיש can simply follow the חכמים. This also prepares the next step, where אביי explains that the dispute is about something else entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause or end part of a משנה
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Say the latter clause:
And the Rabbis say: it is a connection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects רב יוסף's challenge
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the neck-hide line as proof against ריש לקיש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה records a dispute, and the חכמים agree with the outcome ריש לקיש would want.

steps.title: אביי: the dispute is about a protector that comes off easily
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה's dispute has nothing to do with repairable hides. They argue whether a protective covering that tends to come off by itself counts as a שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: They disagree about a protector that tends to come off on its own. One master holds it counts as a protector, and the other holds it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the real explanation of the dispute in the משנה, which removes it from the ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argument altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neck hide hangs loosely and tends to separate on its own. The חכמים say it still counts as a שומר, so it is connected. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says something likely to fall off is not a real protector. Neither side is talking about whether a hide counts as repairable.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective covering, like a peel or hide, that counts as part of the food for טומאה
Likely to come off by itself
They disagree
One master holds

steps.whatToRemember: The neck-hide dispute is about whether a loose שומר counts. It is not about repairable hides, so it neither proves nor disproves ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Regarding a protector that is prone
to come off by itself, they disagree:
one master holds: it is a protector,
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים, who say the neck hide is connected.

phrases.english: and one master holds: it is not a protector.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the quick deflection with a full explanation of the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the dispute is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The neck-hide dispute is about whether an attached, 'repaired' hide counts as connected
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about whether a loose protector that tends to fall off counts as a שומר

steps.title: רבי ירמיה begins a challenge from an impure oven
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה opens a new challenge against ריש לקיש from a משנה about how to purify an impure oven: cut it into three pieces and scrape off the plaster.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objects: An oven that became impure, how is it purified? One divides it into three and scrapes off the plaster...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. רבי ירמיה starts quoting a משנה about an oven, and the point of the challenge comes in the continuation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only hear the method: break the oven into three parts and scrape off its plaster coating. The quote continues beyond this line, and the challenge to ריש לקיש's idea of repairable items will be built from the rest of it.

keyTerms.meaning: An earthenware oven
He divides it into three pieces
Scrapes off
The plaster coating around the oven

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raises an objection:
An oven that became impure,
how does one purify it?
He divides it into three,
and scrapes off the plaster

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fresh challenge to ריש לקיש after the neck-hide challenge was resolved
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that an item that can be repaired still keeps its status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Still being set up: the oven quote continues beyond this line, and the challenge will come from how the broken oven is treated.
